title: Nonnegativity of restriction-event probabilities
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0\le p\le 1$, and let $E$ be a decidable event on restrictions of the $n$ variables. The Bernoulli restriction probability of $E$, formed using the weights $p^{|J|}((1-p)/2)^{n-|J|}$ for a restriction with free-variable set $J$, is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: A decidable event on restrictions of the $n$ variables
replaced:
Let $p \in \bbr$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $E$ be a decidable event on restrictions
of $n$ variables, where a restriction assigns each coordinate either a fixed Boolean
value or leaves it free. Under the Bernoulli($p$)-random restriction --- each
restriction $\rho$ with free-variable set $J$ carries weight
$p^{\abs{J}}\bigl(\tfrac{1-p}{2}\bigr)^{\,n-\abs{J}}$ --- the probability of $E$,
namely the weighted sum of the indicator of $E$ over all restrictions, is nonnegative:
$0 \le \Pr_\rho[E]$.
